scheme_name: Pre Examination Training Centre For All India Service Examinations Like I.A.S., I.P.S., I.R.S., Etc.
description:
The Pre Examination Training Centre for All India Service Examinations is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at providing support to candidates preparing for prestigious civil services examinations such as the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and Indian Revenue Service (IRS) among others.

This scheme was launched in 2006 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance the representation of candidates from marginalized communities in civil services.

The government aims to provide quality training to candidates from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, and economically weaker sections.

The scheme also seeks to improve the success rate of these candidates in the civil services examinations.

The training provided under this scheme includes coaching for preliminary and main examinations.

The training is designed to cover various subjects relevant to the civil services examination syllabus.

The program also includes personality development sessions and interview preparation.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is substantial.

Each training center receives a grant of up to INR 50 lakh for a period of five years.

This funding is intended to cover the costs of infrastructure, faculty salaries, and other operational expenses.

The centers are expected to train a minimum of 200 candidates each year.

The training is provided free of cost to the eligible candidates.

Eligibility for this scheme includes candidates from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes.

Candidates must be graduates or in the final year of their graduation.

There is no specific age limit set for candidates under this scheme.

However, candidates must meet the eligibility criteria set by the Union Public Service Commission for civil services examinations.

The application process for candidates involves several steps.

Interested candidates must apply through the respective training centers.

Each center has its own application form which can be obtained from their official website or office.

Candidates are required to submit proof of their caste and income certificates.

Additionally, candidates must provide their educational qualifications.

The application forms must be submitted before the deadline set by the respective training center.

The training centers are located across various states in India.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment oversees the implementation of this scheme.

The centers are established in collaboration with state governments and non-governmental organizations.

The training sessions typically commence in the month of June each year.

The duration of the training program is usually six months.

Candidates receive a structured timetable outlining the subjects and topics to be covered.

Mock tests and assessments are conducted regularly to evaluate the candidates' progress.

The centers also provide study materials and resources to assist candidates in their preparation.

The disbursement of funds to the training centers is done annually.

The centers are required to submit a utilization certificate to the Ministry for the funds received.

The Ministry conducts periodic reviews to assess the performance of the training centers.

Feedback from candidates is also taken into account to improve the training programs.

Since its inception, the scheme has trained thousands of candidates.

The success rate of candidates who have undergone training has shown a marked improvement.

In the year 2020, approximately 10,000 candidates benefited from this scheme.

The scheme has been instrumental in increasing the number of candidates from underrepresented communities in civil services.

The government has also introduced online training modules to reach a wider audience.

These online modules are designed to complement the physical training provided at the centers.

The initiative reflects the government's commitment to inclusive education and equal opportunities.

The program aligns with the broader goals of the National Education Policy 2020.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to seek partnerships with educational institutions to enhance the quality of training.

The training centers are equipped with modern facilities and experienced faculty members.

Candidates are encouraged to participate in group discussions and interactive sessions.

The centers also organize guest lectures by successful civil servants.

The scheme has received positive feedback from both candidates and educational experts.

In 2021, the government allocated INR 100 crore for the expansion of this scheme.

The expansion includes the establishment of new training centers in underserved regions.

The government aims to increase the number of candidates trained by 25 percent over the next five years.

The program is regularly updated to reflect changes in the civil services examination pattern.

The Ministry also conducts workshops for trainers to enhance their teaching methodologies.

The Pre Examination Training Centre for All India Service Examinations is a vital step towards empowering youth.

It plays a crucial role in bridging the gap between aspirants and opportunities in civil services.

The scheme is a testament to the government's efforts to promote social justice and equality.

Overall, this initiative represents a significant investment in human capital development in India.

The government remains committed to ensuring that all candidates have access to quality training resources.

This scheme is one of many efforts aimed at fostering a more inclusive civil services landscape in India.
